2. Briefly the facts for disposal of the Rule are that the above petitioner as preemptors instituted pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition of the Tenancy Act in the court of Assistant Judge 7th Court, Naogaon for pre-emption of the case land and stated inter alia that the 'ka' scheduled land had recorded in the name Abed Ali Kazi and Shabaj Kazi as per their respective shares. Shabaj Kazi died leaving behind his son Ashraf Ali Kazi and daughter Fatema as his heirs. Abed Ali Kazi died leaving his wife Shrin Bewa, nephew Ashraf, opposite party no.5. Solaiman and I., okinan, who is petitioner no. 1 as his heirs Solaiman Kazi died leaving 2 sons Shahidul, and Opposite Party No.7 and Nazrul, the petitioner No.2 and 3 daughters opposite party nos. 8,9 and 10. Ashraf Kazi died leaving behind 2 sons Aktaruzzaman Hiro, opposite party no.2 and Manik opposite party no.11 and daughters, opposite party no.13 and 14 as heirs. The opposite party no. 2 on 23.6.1999 handed over the case land to opposite party no.1 without the knowledge of the petitioners and that no notice was served on the petitioners. On 23.4.2000 opposite party no.1 disclosed about the matter and the petitioners, thereafter, on 30.4.2000 obtained the certified copy of the transfer deed and came to know about the transfer. The deed in question is not a deed of exchange but it's a kabala deed in consideration of money and the opposite party no.1, in order to frustrate the right of petitioners has created the deed of exchange collusively of the 'ka' schedule land with 'kha' schedule land. The opposite party no. 1 has taken back the 'kha' schedule land on 12.3.2000 in the name of his close relation Naznil Islam and the opposite party no.2 never got the 'kha' schedule land by way of Heba-bil-ewaz and in fact, the deed in question is a kabala deed and as such, the petitioners instituted the case for preemption. 

 4. Opposite party no.1 contested the case by filing written objection and denied the material allegations made in the preemption case and stated further that he got the 'ka' schedule land on 15.1.1994 by way of kabala no. 411 and exchanged his land with the 'ka' schedule land of opposite party no.1 by a registered deed of exchange dated 23.6.1999 and opposite party no. 2 has mortgaged the 'kha' schedule land to the opposite party no. 3 on 13.3.2000 on the basis of return kabala deed and opposite party no. 3 on the same day sworn an affidavit undertaking that he would return the kabala and accordingly returned the land to opposite party no. 2 on 16.5.2000 after getting back the money and opposite party no.2 is now possessing the 'kha' schedule land and as such the case is liable to be dismissed. 

 7. The preemptors again being dissatisfied with the judgment and order of the Appellate court preferred revisional application before this court and having heard the learned Advocate for the petitioners this court issued the rule as stated above. 

 9. Md. Tazul Islam has referred a case reported in 4 MLR (AD) 1999 page 18 and referring to paragraph no.5 submitted that in a similar case their lordships of the Appellate Division found that the courts did not accept the transfer as an exchange but held the transaction is pre-emptible under the provision of Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and in this case the courts below having not held as such committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of Justice. In the above decision their lordships held: "5. Mr. Miah Abdul Gafur, learned Advocate on Record for the petitioner submits that on the very face of the deed in question the transaction is an exchange. The courts below as well as the High Court Division committed an error of law in not holding that the transaction was not pre-emptible under the provisions of section 96 (10) (b) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 1950. Mr. Gafur's submission is not tenable in view of the concurrent finding of the courts below that the transaction is not an exchange but a sale, which has been rightly maintained by the High Court Division. Mr. Gafur next submits that the courts below did not consider that the pre-emptees made considerable improvement in the land in question spending Tk.1,00,000/-. The trial court on consideration of the evidence on record disbelieved the pre-emptees case of improvement which has also been affirmed by the lower appellate court."
